title: Choose the visual world for ReviewRadar
question: The roll assigned Wayfinding Signage. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Crimson stays the brand accent in every option.

options.label: Wayfinding Signage
options.lineage: Swiss transit and airport signage systems
options.thesis: Every screen answers 'where am I, what is my role here, what is waiting for me' like a station sign.
options.viewport: Crimson top band carrying the wordmark, a location line (Projects / project name) and the Inbox count as a numbered square; below, a project list with role pictograms and a right column of invitations waiting for an answer.
options.risk: A solid red band can feel loud if any other surface also uses red heavily; crimson must be rationed below the band.

raised.raise: Length encodes time: each invitation carries a bar whose length is the share of its 7 days still left.
One hairline weight everywhere: every divider and panel edge is the same 1px warm rule, no shadows stacked on borders.
Crimson is rationed below the band: primary action, pending markers and the current location only.
Counts are tabular numerals, right-aligned in their columns.

options.label: Editor's Red Pencil
options.lineage: newsroom proof sheets marked up in red
options.thesis: Reviews are copy to be marked up; crimson is the editor's pencil that circles what needs a decision.
options.viewport: Plain white top bar with a red underline under the current tab; one centred column of projects where pending invitations get a red circle in the margin.
options.risk: Familiar: close to where most clean SaaS redesigns land, and the serif headings drift editorial.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: Almost no colour; crimson appears four times per screen and every panel is a proof.
options.viewport: Thin neutral top bar, two equal panels: your projects and your invitations.
options.case: Holds product clarity, but loses identity: with the name covered it reads as any tool.
options.risk: Grey screen with one accent: the category default without a signature.

options.label: Centre-rail Reference Setting
options.thesis: Two text columns round a rail of keys.
options.viewport: Two narrow columns with a key rail.
options.case: A book page; team members managing access do not read their workspace as an edition.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Shape is direction, length is duration.
options.case: No audience identification and the staff hides the task.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Barcode fields in pure black and white.
options.case: Hostile to calm daily use and to the crimson commitment.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.thesis: Side A / Side B tracklists in ballpoint.
options.case: Nostalgic and playful; wrong register for access control.
options.kept: Timestamps right-aligned tight to the edge.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.case: Hides the list a manager needs to scan.
options.kept: Pending decisions are one action away.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Left sidebar, card grid, crimson primary buttons, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar with Projects / Invitations / Notifications, a 3-column card grid of projects.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other SaaS dashboard, and close to the screenshots you want to move away from.
